SIKA MONOTOP®-436 N: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sika MonoTop®-436 N, April 2023, Version 01.04 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/p/sika-monotop-436n.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sika MonoTop®-436 N where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.04).
1.2 Product description. Sika MonoTop®-436 N is a 1-component pre-bagged, pourable, self-compacting repair mortar meeting the requirements of class R4 of EN 1504-3.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - Suitable for restoration work by recasting (Principle 3, method 3.2 of EN 1504-9).Repair of spalling and damaged concrete in buildings, bridges, infrastructure and superstructure works.
    - Suitable for structural strengthening (principle 4, method 4.4 of EN 1504-9). Increasing the bearing capacity of the concrete structure by adding mortar.
    - Suitable for preserving or restoring passivity (principle 7, method 7.1 and 7.2 of EN 1504-9). Increasing cover with additional mortar and replacing contaminated or carbonated concrete.
    - Beams
    - Balconies
    - Columns
    - Stairs
    - Decks
    - Walls etc.
    Repair of concrete on buildings and civil engineering structures for areas including:
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.9.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sika MonoTop®-436 N
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: R4 HIGH PERFORMANCE, POURABLE MICRO-CONCRETE REPAIR MORTAR
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals / certificates.
    - Qld Roads (TMR) Section 5. Registered and Conforming Products. Part 5.34 Repair Mortars
    - Potable Water approved to AS4020:2018 - Testing of products for use in contact with drinking water
    - RTA Rapid Mortar Bar Test RTA T363 - Alkali Reactive Particles <0.1% (Non-Reactive).
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - EN 1504-3: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Characteristics / Advantages (p.1); Description (p.1).
    - EN 1504-9: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Uses (p.1).
    - AS4020:2018: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - EN 1015-17: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Soluble chloride ion content (p.2).
    - AS 1478.2:2005: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Application Information > Flowability (p.2); Technical Information > Compressive strength (p.2).
    - AS 1012.17: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Modulus of elasticity in compression (p.2).
    - ASTM C 348: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile strength in flexure (p.2).
    - AS 1012.10: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Splitting tensile strength (p.2).
    - EN 1542: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - AS 2350.13: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shrinkage (p.2).
    - EN 12617.4:2002: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Restrained shrinkage / expansion (p.2).
    - EN 1504-2: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Important Considerations (p.3).
    - EN 1504-10: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Important Considerations (p.3).
    - ISO 8501: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Application Instructions > Steel: (p.3).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Class R4 of EN 1504-3
    - Very good flow properties
    - Self compacting micro-concrete
    - Placed from 20mm to 300mm in one pour
    - Chloride Free
    - Carbonation Resistant
    - Excellent adhesion to host Concrete
    - Low water and chloride permeability
    - Low shrinkage
    - Finished surface can be painted after formwork is removed
    - Compatible with Sika® FerroGard® Sacrificial Anode System
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Portland cement, selected aggregates and special additives
    - Appearance and colour: Grey powder
    - Density: Fresh mortar density: ~ 2.3 kg/l
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Maximum grain size: Dmax: 4.0 mm
    - Soluble chloride ion content: ≤ 0.05% (EN 1015-17)
    - Modulus of elasticity in compression: 44.5 GPa at 56 days (AS 1012.17)
    - Splitting tensile strength: 6.5 MPa at 28 days (AS 1012.10)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: > 2.0 MPa (EN 1542)
    - Shrinkage: < 500 microstrains at 28 days (AS 2350.13)
    - Restrained shrinkage / expansion: ≥ 2.0 MPa (EN 12617.4:2002)
2.7 Compressive strength.
    | 1 day | ~ 15 MPa |
    | 7 days | ~ 50 MPa |
    | 28 days | ~ 70 MPa |
    Test method printed: (AS 1478.2:2005)
    Note printed: Material and curing conditions at 23°C / 50% r.h. Above results based on 50mm x 50mm cubes @ 2.5 litres water per 20kg bag
2.8 Tensile strength in flexure.
    | 1 day | > 4 MPa |
    | 7 days | > 10 MPa |
    | 28 days | > 11 MPa |
    Test method printed: (ASTM C 348)
2.9 Electrical resistivity.
    | 7   days | ~ 16,000 Ω.cm |
    | 28 days | ~ 33,000 Ω.cm |
    | 56 days | ~ 44,000 Ω.cm |
    | 90 days | ~ 54,000 Ω.cm |
    Test method printed: (Wenner Probe
    Test method printed: FM5-578)
    Note printed: 50mm Probe Spacing
2.10 System structure. Sika MonoTop®-436 N is a part of system for concrete repair: Bonding Primer / Reinforcement; Corrosion Protection
    | Sika MonoTop® -910N | Normal use |
    | SikaTop® Armatec ®  110 EpoCem® | Demanding requirements |
    | Repair Mortar |
    | Sika MonoTop®-436 N | Structural hand & machine applied |
    | repair |
    | Levelling Mortar |
    | Sika MonoTop®-723 N | Normal use |
    | Sikagard®-720 EpoCem® | Demanding requirements |
    (System build-up table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows. Refer to the data sheet (page 2) for the layout.)
2.11 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 20 kg bags
    - Shelf life: 9 months
    - Storage conditions: Store properly in undamaged original sealed packaging, in dry cool conditions.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.04) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality / pre-treatment - Concrete. The concrete shall be free from dust, loose material, surface contamination and materials which reduce bond or prevent suction or wetting by repair materials. Delaminated, weak, damaged and deteriorated concrete and where necessary sound concrete shall be removed by suitable means.
3.3 Substrate quality / pre-treatment - Steel. Steel reinforcement surface must be free from rust products, mill scale, mortar, concrete residues, oil, grease, dust and other loose materials which may reduce bond or may contribute to corrosion. In case of rust, clean uniformly the whole circumference of the steel bars (where applicable) by using abrasive blast cleaning techniques or high pressure waterblasting to Sa 2 in accordance with ISO 8501. Protect cleaned bars from further contamination, prior to application of the mortar.
3.4 Substrate quality / pre-treatment - Formwork. Formwork necessary for casting shall be of adequate strength, non absorbent, treated with release agent and sealed to prevent mortar leakage. Use SikaSwell®- S2 hydrophilic sealant between any joints. Ensure the formwork design includes outlets for extraction of the pre-wetting water and air.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.04) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: 2.5 to 2.7 litres of water for 20 kg powder
    - Yield: 20 kg of powder yields approximately 9.8 litres of mortar
    - Layer thickness: 20mm min. / 300 mm max.
    - Flowability: > 600mm (Flow trough) (AS 1478.2:2005)
    - Pot Life: ~ 40 minutes at +20°C
    - Initial set time: ~ 4.5 hours
    - Final set time: ~ 7.5 hours
4.3 Mixing. Sika MonoTop®-436 N can be mixed with a low speed (~500 r.p.m.) electrical hand drill mixer with vertical axis for 1 to 2 bags taking care not to entrap air in the mix, or using a force action pan mixer for 2 to 3 bags - or more - at once, depending on the type and size of mixer. Pour the water in the correct desired proportion into a suitable mixing container. While stirring slowly, add the powder gradually in the water and mix thoroughly at least for 3 minutes, adding additional water during the mixing time if necessary up to the maximum specified amount, until the required homogeneous and lump-free consistency is achieved. For larger mixes the mixing time could be extended (up to 5 minutes or as necessary) until the mortar is homogenously mixed with no lumps and no remaining dry powder. Mix full bags for best results. 20 kg of Sika MonoTop®-436 N powder is mixed with 2.5 - 2.7 L of water depending on the required consistency.
4.4 Application - Bonding Primer. On a well prepared and roughened substrate a bonding primer is generally not required. When a bonding primer is not required pre-wet the surface continuously for 2 - 6 hours with clean water. Immediately before casting remove all water from formwork. The surface shall not be allowed to totally dry before application of the concrete repair mortar. The surface shall achieve a dark matt appearance without glistening and surface pores and pits shall not contain water (saturated surface dry-SSD) condition.
4.5 Application - Reinforcement Corrosion Protection. Where a reinforcement coating is required as a barrier (e.g. in case of insufficient concrete cover), apply to the whole exposed circumference two coats of Sika MonoTop®-910 N or SikaTop® 110 EpoCem® (Refer to the relevant Product Data Sheet).
4.6 Application - Pouring / Filling. The product should be poured directly on the wet mat substrate or inside the formwork prepared for the casting. By using more than one mixer and with the proper organization, you can pour the fresh material reducing construction joints. After mixing Sika MonoTop®-436 N, leave the mortar to stand for ~1-2 minutes; stir again with a trowel and then pour immediately into sealed, rigid - stable prepared formworks. To make optimum use of the product's expansion properties apply the mortar as quickly as possible (within max. 15 minutes). Pot life shall also be taken into consideration, adjusting for weather conditions, when planning the work duration.
4.7 Curing treatment.
    - Protect the fresh mortar from early dehydration using the relevant curing method.
    - Cure for a minimum of 7 days to minimise cracking. Use a 90% efficient curing membrane or polythene sheeting taped down at the edges.
4.8 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with water immediately after use. Hardened / cured material can only be removed mechanically.
4.9 Limitations and important considerations.
    - For carbonation resistance use a coating complying with EN 1504-2
    - Apply only to prepared sound surfaces
    - Avoid application in direct sun and/or strong wind
    - Do not add water over recommended dosage
    - Only prepare quantity of material which can be handled within pot life time
    - Do not use vibrators for compaction
    - Protect freshly applied material from freezing
    - Do not add additional water during the surface finishing as this will cause discoloration and cracking
    - Refer to Qualified Engineer for any movement, expansion or cold joint positions
    - Do not use a curing agent if coatings are to be applied
    - Refer to the Method Statement for Concrete Repair using Sika MonoTop® system for more information regarding substrate preparation or refer to the recommendations in EN 1504-10

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +5 °C minimum; +30 °C maximum
5.3 Substrate temperature. +5 °C minimum; +30 °C maximum
5.4 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.9):
    - Avoid application in direct sun and/or strong wind
    - Protect freshly applied material from freezing
5.5 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Soluble chloride ion content: ≤ 0.05% (EN 1015-17)
    - Compressive strength: 1 day | ~ 15 MPa; 7 days | ~ 50 MPa; 28 days | ~ 70 MPa (AS 1478.2:2005)
    - Modulus of elasticity in compression: 44.5 GPa at 56 days (AS 1012.17)
    - Tensile strength in flexure: 1 day | > 4 MPa; 7 days | > 10 MPa; 28 days | > 11 MPa (ASTM C 348)
    - Splitting tensile strength: 6.5 MPa at 28 days (AS 1012.10)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: > 2.0 MPa (EN 1542)
    - Shrinkage: < 500 microstrains at 28 days (AS 2350.13)
    - Restrained shrinkage / expansion: ≥ 2.0 MPa (EN 12617.4:2002)
    - Electrical resistivity: 7   days | ~ 16,000 Ω.cm; 28 days | ~ 33,000 Ω.cm; 56 days | ~ 44,000 Ω.cm; 90 days | ~ 54,000 Ω.cm (Wenner Probe FM5-578)
    - Flowability: > 600mm (Flow trough) (AS 1478.2:2005)
5.6 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.7 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sika MonoTop®-436 N, April 2023, Version 01.04, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/p/sika-monotop-436n.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sika MonoTop 436 N AU, version 15/07/2024, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/w/MSDS%20Sika%20MonoTop-436N%20AU%20GHS7.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: sds-sika-monotop-436nau, https://aus.sika.com/dms/getdocument.get/dd8f819f-e90a-441e-9b08-6eeac6a8a8ab_au01/sds-sika-monotop-436nau.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
